It resolves a class list through its module-level constant, which is how five of the seven sites hid inside one ICON_BTN string, and it walks JSX tags brace-aware, because a handler containing => truncates the tag and drops every attribute after it - the reason an earlier scan in this same lane missed the header cluster on its first pass. column5: FIXED (commit efa75725f), the link row's height. THE RULE: src/index.css floors every button, a and [role=button] at min-height/min-width 44px inside @media (max-width: 768px) unless the element carries no-min-size. That query covers BOTH narrow boards - 375, and 768 itself, because max-width is inclusive and Tailwind md: (min-width: 768px) begins at the same pixel - and min-height beats height on the cascade whatever the order or specificity, so a control's own size class cannot undercut it. A class scan cannot see this: the size class is present either way and the floor wins anyway. TokenSocialLinks.tsx's own header records the row MEASURED off 14259:216621 on this board at 343x24, three 110.33 columns on a 6px gap. Each cell is an <a>, none carried no-min-size, so the row painted 44 tall - 83% over the 24 the file itself writes down. no-min-size added; touchFloorOptOuts.test.tsx resolves the rule (it lifts the real selector list out of index.css, injects it without the media wrapper since jsdom has no viewport width, and reads minHeight back off the anchor, with a bare button appended as the negative control) and reads 44px against the previous value.
